ids.sargon-of-akkad: A gardener's foster son who became the first emperor in history.
ids.hammurabi: The king of Babylon who carved his laws in stone for everyone to read.
ids.ramesses-ii: Egypt's showman pharaoh: warrior, builder, and maker of the oldest known peace treaty.
ids.cyrus-the-great: The founder of the Persian Empire, remembered by friends and enemies alike as a just king.
ids.darius-i: The organiser of the Persian Empire, whose royal couriers inspired the US Postal Service's motto.
ids.cleopatra: The last queen of ancient Egypt, who outwitted Rome for twenty years.
ids.pericles: The leader of Athens in its golden age, who built the Parthenon.
ids.socrates: The barefoot questioner of Athens, who chose death over silence.
ids.plato: Socrates' pupil, who founded the Academy and wrote philosophy's most famous books.
ids.aristotle: Alexander the Great's teacher, who wrote about almost everything and founded logic and biology.
ids.alexander-the-great: He conquered an empire from Greece to India before he was 33, and never lost a battle.
ids.hannibal: The Carthaginian general who crossed the Alps with elephants and nearly brought down Rome.
ids.pompey: Rome's greatest general before Caesar, and Caesar's partner, then rival.
ids.julius-caesar: The general who conquered Gaul, crossed the Rubicon, and was stabbed on the Ides of March.
ids.mark-antony: Caesar's right-hand man, Cleopatra's lover, and Octavian's great rival.
ids.augustus: Rome's first emperor, who found the city brick and left it marble.
ids.gautama-buddha: A prince who gave up his palace to find the end of suffering, and woke up.
ids.ashoka: The conqueror who was horrified by his own war and became a king of peace.
ids.confucius: China's great teacher, whose ideas on family and good government shaped East Asia.
ids.qin-shi-huang: The First Emperor, who united China and was buried with an army of clay.
ids.leonardo-da-vinci: The painter of the Mona Lisa, who filled notebooks with machines no one could yet build.
ids.isaac-newton: The farm boy who found the rules that move the planets.
ids.ludwig-van-beethoven: He wrote the world's most famous symphonies, the greatest of them after he had gone deaf.
ids.archimedes: The greatest mathematician of the ancient world, who shouted "Eureka!"
ids.euclid: The father of geometry, whose textbook was used for 2,000 years.
ids.pythagoras: The mystery man of numbers, whose theorem every student learns.
ids.moses: The prophet who, in the Bible's story, led his people out of slavery in Egypt.
ids.laozi: The old master of the Way, who wrote a little book and rode off into the west.
ids.sun-tzu: The general whose Art of War is still read by soldiers, coaches and business leaders.
ids.zhang-qian: The envoy who walked into the unknown west and opened the way for the Silk Road.
ids.khufu: The pharaoh behind the Great Pyramid, the last Wonder of the Ancient World still standing.
ids.hatshepsut: The queen who made herself pharaoh, and the stepson who tried to erase her from history.
ids.tutankhamun: A boy pharaoh who ruled briefly, and whose untouched tomb made him the most famous of them all.
ids.leonidas-i: The Spartan king who held the pass at Thermopylae with 300 men.
ids.spartacus: The gladiator who led a slave army against Rome.
